hints.title: Per-Tier Maximum Obstacle
hints.text: Each row corresponds to a specific depth level in the binary tree. How can isolating each level during traversal allow computing the maximum value among all nodes at that depth?

hints.title: Level Snapshot Invariant
hints.text: Process the tree level by level. At each tier, initialize the tier maximum to negative infinity and update it with every node in that tier.

hints.title: Breadth-First Row Maximum Procedure
hints.text: If root is null, return empty list. Initialize a queue with root. While queue is non-empty, record tier size, set max_val to -infinity, pop all nodes of that tier, update max_val = max(max_val, node.val), and enqueue children. Append max_val to results.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: number of nodes in tree (0 <= N <= 10^4)
complexity.notes: Standard level order queue traversal taking the maximum over each tier in linear time.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: DFS traversal requires tracking an auxiliary array indexed by depth, which is identical in asymptotic cost.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Initializing tier maximum to negative infinity to support negative node values.
